case_title: Suraj Jagannath Jadha v. The State of Maharashtra
aggravating_circumstances: Fully conscious of the dangerous nature of the act, intentional infliction of harm, absence of provocation
neutral_facts: The accused, who was married to the victim, poured kerosene on her while she was attempting to escape from the house. He then lit a matchstick and set her ablaze. The victim sustained severe burns and later died from the injuries. The accused was not under the influence of alcohol at the time of the incident. The victim's dying declaration indicated that the accused was fully conscious of the dangerous nature of his actions. The accused attempted to extinguish the fire by pouring water on the victim after she had already been set ablaze. The prosecution relied on the victim's dying declaration and medical evidence to establish the sequence of events and the intent behind the accused's actions.
